steps.prompt: Redraw the character in this reference image as a labelled 3 by 3 grid of nine puppet heads. Keep the character exactly as the reference shows it — same colours, same fur or skin texture, same eyes, same ears, same muzzle, same headwear, same art style — and change nothing but the mouth. Nine cells in three even rows of three on one flat uniform mid-grey ground: the same head at the same size, upright, front-facing and centred in every cell, with clear grey between the cells so that no two heads touch. Each head differs from the others only in the shape of its mouth. Under each head, in the empty grey below it and clear of the ears, print that cell's short mouth-shape label in plain grey capitals. The nine mouth shapes, in reading order left to right and top to bottom, are: a, o, e, wr, ts, ln, uq, mbp, fv. Those codes are phonetic, and no two of the nine may look alike: a is a wide open jaw, o is a small tight round pucker, e is a wide open smile shape, wr is rounded and pushed forward, ts is a narrow slit showing the teeth, ln shows the tongue tip up behind open teeth, uq is a very small tight pucker, mbp is the lips fully pressed shut with no opening at all, and fv is the top teeth resting on the lower lip. Flat solid uniform grey background, no gradient, no drop shadows, no cell borders or grid lines, no other text.

fields.visemes: a, o, e, wr, ts, ln, uq, mbp, fv
